notes.title: v1.0.9
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! We're back with another patch for [i]MonCon[/i]. Version 1.0.9 fixes a lot of user-reported bugs & bugs from our own backlog:

[list]
[*] Cleaned up flaky logic surrounding Marnie's interview section of the afternoon chapter. In particular, there was a specific order of events that could cause the game to softlock if you talk to Marnie after the interviews, but before beginning Joey's first shadow work section; this has been fixed.
[*] Improved NPC path-finding logic
[*] Fixed bug where room music would not resume playing if you talk to a fuzzy in one of the hotel hallways
[*] Fixed bug where NPCs could initially appear without costumes if you defeated first enemy in battle but then subsequently ran away
[*] Fixed bug where camera would not return to default position when selling at a shopkeep after closing your inventory
[*] Fixed bug where removing Fambox cartridge would simultaneously cause HUD menu to drop down when playing with a controller
[*] Disabled phone/inventory interaction while inside the running section of shadow work
[*] Added an autosave point after the end of the evening chapter's dungeon, but before the start of the after-midnight chapter of the game
[*] Force capital letters on in-game keyboard when using gamepad in the second dungeon, or on the Duck Claw password screen
[*] Don't allow player to repeatedly buy the same phone app, or buy smaller backpacks after increasing backpack size
[*] Fixed graphical bug where colors would not immediately update in the third dungeon
[*] Fixed graphical bug where player costumes would not immediately update in certain rooms in the third dungeon
[/list]

notes.title: v1.0.8
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! It's time for another [i]MonCon [/i] bugfix patch! We're getting very close to the end of our list of known serious bugs.

Here's what's been fixed this week:

[list]
[*]  Fixed bug where fighting multiple enemies and trying to run away with the self-pity ailment could crash the game
[*]  Fixed bug where opening an inventory in battle, using the phone to call another character, and then trying to re-open the original inventory could cause the game to crash
[*]  Fixed bug where assertive-personality characters can soft-lock the game by talking to you in the after-midnight section
[*]  Fixed gameplay bug where an item in the finale section was reachable through a collision wall
[*]  Fixed graphical bug where Zoey could appear twice onscreen during Marnie's interviews in the afternoon section
[/list]

notes.title: v1.0.7
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! v1.0.7 of [i]MonCon [/i]is here!

We'd received some feedback that some of the timings for the attack button patterns were a bit sloppy and didn't line up well with the music. This patch concentrates on tightening up all the attacks throughout the game, but we did our best to not fundamentally alter the experience we were going for with each attack.

Additionally, some of the attack button patterns were unnecessarily dense for easy mode (the only mode available right now). We've reserved the more complex button patterns for normal and hard modes, which will become available in future patches.

Thanks again to everyone for your support!

notes.title: v1.0.6
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! I didn't have as much time this week to address [i]MonCon [/i]bugs, so there's still a few reported problems which are not addressed in this build. Nonetheless, please take a quick gander at what's new in this release!

[list]
[*] Fixed a game-crashing bug during the final boss battle.
[*] Fixed a bug that would prevent music from playing during the final chapter.
[*] Fixed a variety of bugs related to the Marnie interview battle gauntlet in the afternoon chapter of the game.
[*] Fixed some graphical bugs related to where Joey would position himself in certain rooms when saving the game.
[*] Added an effect to the "Calm of the Whale" omamori that reduces the intensity of Marnie's angry dragon phases.
[/list]

notes.title: v1.0.5
notes.notes:
We're back with another patch release for [i]MonCon[/i]! We knocked out a lot of little bugs with this release, and also added a few minor QoL features:

[list]
[*]  Fixed bug where multiple second player ships could be created when playing [i]Space Party[/i] minigame and returning from a Game Over
[*]  Fixed bug where consuming food/drink in battle would not alleviate appropriate ailments
[*]  Fixed bug where you could waste suitcase keys on already-unlocked suitcases
[*]  Fixed bug where NPCs could cause collision problems by overlapping the player's screen position while they're in the middle of saving the game
[*]  Fixed bug where NPCs could occasionally spawn on top of walls or other NPCs when a new room is loaded
[*]  Fixed bug where inventory cursor could end up one cell outside of the inventory while looking into a suitcase and swapping player inventories
[*]  Fixed bug where player would not be rewarded after the boss battle from the afternoon chapter of the game
[*]  Fixed controller bug that prevented D-pad from being used for player movement
[*]  Fixed a variety of bugs related to boss battles in the after-midnight chapter of the game
[*]  Fixed a variety of bugs related to suitcase loading in the latter half of the game (evening and after-midnight)
[*]  Fixed graphical bug where inventories and suitcases would flicker for one frame on the screen before sliding in
[*]  Fixed graphical bug where Marnie's confidence points would disappear after becoming angry dragon
[*]  Fixed graphical bug where inventory item descriptions could run off the screen during battles
[*]  Fixed graphical bug where shop UI would not extend for longer item names
[*]  Fixed graphical bug relating to forklift in second dungeon after saving the game and re-loading
[*]  Fixed graphical bug relating to missing zbuffer in third dungeon
[*]  Added gliding up/down movement to Bulletin Board app
[*]  Added more medium/low options for shaders
[/list]
As always, thanks for your patience, and thanks for your help in finding these bugs!

notes.title: v1.0.4
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! Here comes another small patch for MonCon! As we continue to plow through our list of semi-serious known issues, here's what we got fixed this week:

 - Various graphical & usability improvements for the Trading Expert phone app - this app should be [i]much[/i] easier to navigate now!
 - Fixed bug where autosave file would keep unnecessary "cruft" from previous saves
 - Fixed a graphical bug in room 709 that occurs at the chapter boundary between evening and after-midnight
 - Graphics, text, and battle logic improvements to various boss battles in the after-midnight section of the game

notes.title: v1.0.3
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! It's time for the next MonCon bugfix! This patch gets us [i]all caught up[/i] on issues reported by users:

[list]
[*] Fixed game crash if any shop runs out of items
[*] Fixed bug where Eye of the Eagle omamori wouldn't work if Masked Mystery enemy reveals itself in battle, or if an enemy calls for help
[*] Fixed bug where Joey's battle sprite would start sliding diagonally across the screen if player's HP drops to zero during Karl's tutorial battle
[*] Fixed bug that would prevent Run Boy speedrun leaderboard from updating during the afternoon in the Panel Room B
[*] Fixed bug where spamming 'A' to try to get back into the Run Boy speedrun competition will occasionally prevent the speedrun timer from starting
[*] Fixed bug where Owen can be repeatedly added to your team list if you keep re-entering the room 
where you find him (afternoon/evening sections only)
[*] Fixed cutscene bug where Joey walks into the table and gets stuck after reuniting Owen with his mom in the afternoon section
[*] Fixed controller bug where walking against walls could occasionally cause Joey to "teleport" to the other side of the room
[*] The bug fixed in 1.0.2 (your list of teammates could get mangled under certain circumstances after getting Game Over) caused a variety of downstream problems that have also been fixed:

[list]
[*] A game crash if you attend a panel
[*] If you get overwhelmed after your party members leave, they still get reloaded into your party
[*] If you go talk to one of your party members after the previous bug, you can get duplicate party members

notes.title: v1.0.2
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! It's time for the next MonCon bugfix! This patch fixes a number of issues reported by users:

[list]
[*] Fixed game crash if you talk to the Bravo Bus shopkeep more than once (caused by typo)
[*] Fixed intermittent bug with how the team member list is saved / loaded if you get Game Over in a battle
[*] Fixed display bug where Joey's name appears (instead of player's custom name) when selling items
[*] Fixed display bug where certain battle ailments result in hidden button lanes if playing on a monitor resolution larger than MonCon's native 1080p
[*] Made it more obvious that the player needs to hold (not press) the exit button in order to exit minigames
[/list]

Thanks for all the bug reports - they've been super helpful! While I haven't had time to address everything that's been reported yet, rest assured it's all documented on my master bug backlog, and I'm marching down the list as fast as I can.

And last but not least, thanks for all the positive encouragement about the game so far! It really means a lot!

notes.title: v1.0.1
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! A few players have already found bugs (especially towards the end of the game), so I wanted to go ahead and push out a first patch today to get some of that resolved. Mild spoilers in the patch notes, so read at your own peril.

[list]
[*] Fixed game crash in same after-midnight section if you have a particular character in your party
[*] Fixed game crash if you use the attack menu scrollbar in the Contacts phone app, and then switch to another party member who doesn't have the scrollbar displayed
[*] Fixed game crash if you use AAAAAA batteries without Marnie in your party
[*] Fixed bug where you could get stuck on the third floor of the convention hall in the after-midnight section
[*] Fixed bug where you could accidentally start the wrong cutscene in room 606 during the after-midnight section

notes.title: MonCon Livestream + Q&A
notes.notes:
During this livestream event, I'll be playing through the latest build of MonCon - showing off brand-new story content - and I'll be answering questions from anyone tuned in!

[b]The Story[/b]

MonCon is the story of Joey, a young teenager struggling with social anxiety. Joey decides to attend one of the largest geek culture conventions in the world, in the hopes of meeting his hero - legendary game designer Mr. Miyashiro - and getting an autograph.

For Joey, a normal conversation feels like a fight to the death. Through his eyes, ordinary people transform into hideous monsters that must be verbally battled to survive.

But with the help of his newfound friends, Joey will start to overcome his social hang-ups, and learn that not everyone you meet is a monster.

[i]MonCon is expected to ship Q1 2024.[/i]

notes.title: MonCon Newsletter #11 - UNWINDING FROM CSGC!
notes.notes:
Greetings, one and all! It's time for your every-once-in-a-while scoop of MonCon development information! Progress on the game is still trundling along at a healthy pace. But before we get down into the nitty-gritty of where the game is at, let's briefly reminisce about the fun we all had at CSGC...

[h3]CSGC = Completely Super Gaming Convention[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39217112/c2f4735461eb2abd1504e6081e08a8c33593fa07.png[/img]

Ok, that's not at all what it stands for, but that pretty accurately captures our feelings about the event. Formerly the Heartland Gaming Expo, CSGC is one of our favorite conventions to attend, and not just because it's local and doesn't involve lugging all our crap to another city. It's also [url=https://www.facebook.com/media/set/?set=a.486321464857573&type=3]the very first convention[/url] that Anton and I ever attended to show off [i]The Idiot's Tale[/i] way back in 2015. This was our seventh year in attendance, and they haven't kicked us out yet for exhibiting too many times, so CSGC 2024 is already on the calendar as far as we're concerned!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39217112/035bc9e53c31e1b7a96adb093976e06914640ad0.png[/img]

If you're local to the Tulsa area, I highly recommend stopping by next year. We had a blast talking to everyone and watching people get to play the new build of [i]MonCon[/i] (and find some bugs for us!)

[h3]Now on to the MonCon progress update...[/h3]

As you can see, Chapter 3 of the game is mostly complete. A huge chunk of time over the last couple of months was spent on [b]completely rewiring the NPC character creation system.[/b] While it's always annoying to have to go back and redo work, it was a worthwhile investment. In the past, each NPC had to be meticulously created by hand, but the new system allows us to create NPCs much faster. It's something like one of those character creators you'd see in a triple-A game where you can cycle through a hundred different sets of eye types until you find that absolutely perfect eyeball that expresses you.

Anyway, where was I? Oh yeah, designing NPCs is much faster now. This means that work on the remainder of the game will also be faster.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39217112/d6e415bd516fd65cd4693161ca1fe154be379351.png[/img]

Since we're in the last stages of Chapter 3 development, this involves creating art assets and adding the last little bits of polish to give MonCon that extra oomph in the quality department. We've been working with our composer, and have new pieces of ambient music for Chapter 3, as well as brand-new battle attack songs that we can't wait for you guys to hear.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39217112/6d5663acac6d2b7b09a2da0ebf92c5d8fb1476d2.png[/img]

As far as what lies ahead, we have two more upcoming conventions - both of them in June, one physical, and one digital. There's the [url=https://www.nescatunga.org/]Nescatunga Arts Festival[/url] in Alva, Oklahoma, happening from June 2nd to June 4th. We'll have an [i][b]even more complete build[/b][/i] of [i]MonCon[/i] for people to play.

Secondly, we'll also be participating in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/nextfest]Steam Next Fest[/url] this year. There will be at least one livestream where we show off [i]MonCon[/i] gameplay and answer questions from YOU, the fans! Be sure to [url=https://twitter.com/MonconRpg]follow us on social media[/url] to get the latest and greatest updates about both these events.

Don't forget you can still join the [url=https://discord.gg/86dx5Uw]MonCon Discord server[/url] to meet up with other MonCon fans online!

That's all for now!
Until next time!

~ Elliott

notes.title: MonCon Newsletter #10
notes.notes:
Well, here we are at the end of 2022! It's hard to believe I've been working on MonCon on and off for close to five years now. This past year has definitely seen the most amount of steady progress on the game.

I have some cool new content to share, but before we get too far down into the weeds, I'll let you guys in on this newsletter's big announcement:

[i][b]MonCon will be coming out by the end of 2023![/b][/i]

I've finished enough this year that I feel safe drawing this line in the sand. 2023 will still be a tight race to the finish line, but I think that this deadline strikes a good balance between getting the game out in a reasonable amount of time so that I can move on to other projects, and not compromising on the game's overall quality.

So by hook or by crook, come hell or high water, the full version of MonCon will be in your hands by this time next year.

Now, let's consult the progress chart and see where things are at:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39217112/2732521e51c51d9a54a96339b54fdc043f0f2374.png[/img]

As you can see, the game's side-quests are mostly done! Right now, I'm working with a secondary writer for the rest of the side-quest content. My goal in doing this is to really cement that eclectic "melting pot" vibe that you get when attending a convention, and bringing in a second writing voice should really help with that. But working with outside help means that a fraction of the game's cutscenes and quests are still cooking in the pipeline.

Meanwhile, MonCon's arcade minigames are also coming along nicely. I've settled on a grand total of eleven minigames for the final game. Seven of those are complete, but the remaining four should have a fairly short development cycle, as they'll mostly be reskins / tweaks / advanced versions of the existing minigames.

Here's a peek at one of the brand-new minigames I just put the finishing touches on:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39217112/105b639e8d4084e8d637c3fc94335b39e64b22e0.png[/img]

I've also begun working on brand new monsters you'll have to conversation-battle in the later chapters of the game. There are a lot of new monster designs that I can't wait for you all to see! Here's a few that you'll have to converse with in Chapter 3...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39217112/c336706f2835d9d6d90c07c363ad86b24a5d370a.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39217112/61d6c4df448c9ee7a35c7dcdad38c281de61ac2e.png[/img]

Last but not least, I wanted to give everyone a convention-related update. As per our usual tradition, we will be attending CSGC in Tulsa, Oklahoma in April. This time around, we will have a brand-new build of MonCon that will be feature-complete up to the end of Chapter 3, AKA the first 40% or so of the game. This goes far beyond any public demo of MonCon I've ever shown at previous conventions. If you're in the area, you'll definitely want to drop by to check out all the new game content.

And that's it for now! Wishing everyone safe winter travels, and we'll talk again in the new year!

That's all for now!

Happy New Year!

~ Elliott

notes.title: MonCon Newsletter #9
notes.notes:
It's time for another MonCon progress update!

This newsletter will be on the shorter side, as I'm just dropping by to let everyone know that the game is still making steady progress. But first, I want to get a bit of bad news out of the way...

For most of 2022, I had been dropping subtle hints about "big news" that I'd be able to announce soon. Well, that "big news" unfortunately didn't materialize as hoped, so I'll just go ahead and tell everyone what happened: MonCon had acquired a publisher.

I had begun working with said publisher earlier in the spring, and we'd come to an agreement that they'd help me localize the game and release it onto consoles. Sadly, that publishing deal fell through, so I'm back to just working on finishing the game solo. It was definitely a disappointing setback, but it hasn't deterred me from soldiering on to finish the game.

Anyway! Here's where we're at on the big ol' progress chart:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39217112/b6600505f79c00bfd65dcb726517d40fe174d23e.png[/img]

As you can see, since the last newsletter two months ago, I've finished writing almost all of the game's "major" cutscenes and quests. This would be everything you have to see and do in order to finish the game. I've decided to hold off writing Chapter 6 (aka the climax of the game) for the time being, because, well, the ending is still a little undecided for me. I know all the major beats of what will happen, but the particulars of how I want to land this plane are still eluding me (for now anyway).

The red "Cutscenes & Puzzles" bar has now been split in two, so that I can also show progress on all the sub-quests that don't actually pertain to finishing the game. There will be a plethora of little fun things for you to do around MonCon besides moving towards your ultimate goal of getting an audience with the legendary Mr. Miyashiro. As of today, I've completed most of the work for the sub-quests that will occur during Chapter 3.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39217112/ee1d170211639fc9b8238d8c17dbb7b7f4bec836.png[/img]

Most of the speedy game development I'm getting to enjoy now has been made possible by a brand-new master debug screen that I've added to the game's code to help me work faster:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39217112/b2b5c944e95fbfed465eaf90ed8b2b13344c6491.png[/img]

This debug screen lets me control the game's state (i.e. Which quests have been completed? What chapter am I on?), as well as add or remove team members, add or remove inventory items, and toggle which NPCs have already been defeated in battle. It was a solid day of work to get this screen implemented, but the time savings for being able to teleport around the game at will, with any item, any teammate, to any point in the story? Those time savings have been immense. I definitely wouldn't be able to chuck extra sub-quests into the game as quickly as I am without this debug screen.

To any other game developers out there that may be reading this newsletter: these types of debug screens are a huge boon for quick development, and I highly recommend taking the time to implement one for your own project.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39217112/f2ceba9fe57c6e31a4b685eb739ef1eeb4b5f1f4.png[/img]

Now, even with all the strides I've made this fall towards finishing the game, it's looking like a 2022 release date is not happening at this point. On the plus side, I'm fairly confident that enough of MonCon will be finished by next spring that I'll have a new, longer demo to take to the convention circuit in 2023. I'll keep you all posted on that.

---

Don't forget you can still join the [url=https://discord.gg/86dx5Uw]MonCon Discord server[/url] to meet up with other MonCon fans online!

That's all for now!

Until next time!
 ~ Elliott
